topic: The Physics of Refraction: Why Light Bends

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Nature of Light Waves
lecture_lines: Light travels as a constant wave in a vacuum.
Optical density measures how a medium slows light down.
Denser materials cause light to slow down significantly.
animations: Fade in a white (#FFFFFF) sine wave moving left to right.
Highlight the wave path with a cyan (#00FFFF) glow.
Animate a vertical shift to show slowing in a dense medium (red #FF0000).

sections.title: Defining Refraction and Snell's Law
lecture_lines: Refraction occurs when light changes direction between media.
Snell's Law predicts this change mathematically.
We measure angles relative to the normal line.
animations: Draw a ray hitting a boundary with a normal line (white #FFFFFF).
Show the ray bending and label the formula n1*sin(theta1) = n2*sin(theta2) (yellow #FFFF00).
Animate theta1 and theta2 labels to show relative angles.

sections.title: The Refractive Index (n)
lecture_lines: Refractive index describes material optical density.
Higher index means slower light speed.
Higher index also causes more bending.
animations: Display n = c/v (yellow #FFFF00) in the center.
Fade in n > 1 as a property for water (blue #0000FF).
Show a high-index medium causing sharp ray deflection (red #FF0000).

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Archer Fish
lecture_lines: Archer fish navigate refraction to catch prey.
Light bends at the water's surface.
The fish compensates for the apparent position.
animations: Draw an archer fish (white #FFFFFF) beneath the water surface.
Animate a light ray bending from prey to the fish.
Display dashed lines showing the apparent vs true position (cyan #00FFFF).

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Light changes direction when speed changes.
Refraction depends on the refractive index.
The normal line is our reference point.
animations: Show a summary list of speed changes in different media.
Final animation of a ray refracting through a prism (white #FFFFFF).
